messages:
Elaine (Docs): Heads-up — I'm updating the 'usage heuristics' export docs. Need clarity on heatmap export semantics for burst credits and tier attribution when customers change tiers mid-window. Draft snippet pasted below. Can analytics/billing confirm?

Elaine (Docs): ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
# export tokens by tier as a CSV heatmap for Jan 2026
csv = client.usage.export_heatmap(start='2026-01-01', end='2026-01-31', group_by='tier')
print(csv)
```

Elaine (Docs): Questions: 1) Should burst credits show up in the 'available' column or added into 'used'? 2) If a customer downgrades mid-window, how do we attribute tokens to tiers in the report?

Sahil (Eng-Platform): Quick note — backend supports include_burst=True flag which adds burst consumption into 'used'. Default is False. Tier attribution historically used allocation_at_window_start, but a recent platform PR added prorate=true behavior (opt-in). Tina can confirm current analytics semantics.

Tina (Analytics): Confirmed: include_burst toggles whether burst tokens are aggregated into the 'used' column. Attribution: by default reports use allocation at window start. If prorate=true we pro-rate usage across tier changes within the window (we use time-weighted allocation). See internal runbook: https://confluence.internal/redwood/exports-heuristics (internal link).

Michael (Billing): For invoices we always charge against the committed/billed tier (post-invoice adjustments handled separately). Docs should clearly call out 'reporting view vs billing view' so customers don't confuse the heatmap with their invoice. Suggest a short example showing both views side-by-side. :+1:

Julia (DevEx): I can update the SDK snippet to include include_burst and prorate flags and add a curl example. Will add a small unit test snippet too. Any preferred phrasing for the billing vs reporting callout?

Elaine (Docs): Proposed wording: "The heatmap export is a reporting artifact. It can include burst credits when include_burst=true. Tier attribution follows the allocation at the start of the reporting window unless prorate=true is set to enable time-weighted attribution. Billing follows committed tier post-invoice and may differ from the reporting view." OK to use that?

Sahil (Eng-Platform): lgtm. Also add a tiny CSV example showing prorate.

Tina (Analytics): Sample CSV row for the docs: `2026-01-10,allocation_tier=pro,prorate=0.75,tokens=75000` — indicates 75% of the window on pro.

Michael (Billing): :thumbsup: Also call out rounding behavior — we round token pro-rates up to the nearest token for reporting.

Elaine (Docs): Great. I'll add both Python and curl examples, the billing note, and the CSV sample. I'll open a PR once Julia adds the SDK param example.

Julia (DevEx): PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/3345 — includes SDK snippet, curl example, and a tiny test. Requesting reviewers: @Sahil @Tina @Michael

Sahil (Eng-Platform): Reviewing now. One nit: use group_by='allocation_tier' in the snippet to avoid ambiguity.

Tina (Analytics): Good catch — please switch to allocation_tier. Also add a short note about timezone used (UTC).

Elaine (Docs): Fixed draft to allocation_tier and added UTC note. Final check: add both SDK v1/v2 examples? I can add v2 as a second snippet.

Michael (Billing): curl example is useful for compliance orgs. Keep v1 python first, curl second, v2 example last.

Elaine (Docs): Perfect — will merge after approvals. Thanks everyone :rocket:
